title: Hotel Rate Parity — input

hotelNames.title: Properties by name
hotelNames.description: Hotel names, e.g. ["Hyatt Regency Lisbon"]. Google search plus a name-overlap guard rejects weak matches, but does not verify identity. Check hotel_name, hotel_url and entity_id before using the comparison. No match gives a free not_found status row. Reuse a verified entity_id in hotels for repeat checks; names and a city can be ambiguous. A Google entity response and a result-list response use different overlap thresholds.

hotels.title: Properties (Google Hotels URLs or entity tokens)
hotels.description: Exact hotels by Google Hotels URL (https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/entity/ChkI…) or entity token, e.g. the entity_id of a row from an earlier run or from kestrel/google-hotels-prices. No search: one offers call per hotel and stay, nothing unrelated is ever billed. Use to check the SAME hotels every morning (your property and its comp set): resolve names once, then pass their entity_id values here. Names belong in hotelNames.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.description: Check-in date: "2026-11-02" (YYYY-MM-DD), or relative to the day the run starts: "30 days", "6 weeks", "+30d", "today", "tomorrow". Use relative dates for a schedule ("check parity daily"): the input never needs editing and every run looks the same distance ahead. A past date is rejected before anything is charged. Required.

nights.title: Nights
nights.description: Length of stay in nights, 1 to 30, e.g. 2 (default 1). Check-out = check-in + nights. Every source's rate in the row is for this exact stay and occupancy.

sweepDays.title: Sweep check-in over N more days
sweepDays.description: 0 (default) = only the stay above. N = also check the same length of stay starting on each of the next N days, e.g. 6 = 7 check-in dates per hotel, one row each. Use for "next week", "the weekend", "a rate calendar", "the next 30 days" (29). Every stay is billed as its own row, so cost × (N + 1): 5 hotels × sweepDays 6 = 35 rows = $0.35. Maximum 60.

minSpreadPct.title: Only keep spreads of at least N %
minSpreadPct.description: 0 (default) keeps every priced stay. N filters cheapest-to-dearest spread_pct, NOT the OTA discount from direct. For "OTA undercuts direct by 5%", keep 0; downstream require official_price not null, undercut_by nonempty and undercut_pct >= 5. Missing official_price means unknown, not parity passed. Source minima can differ in room, cancellation, meal or tax terms; a price gap alone is not a verified equivalent-rate breach. Filtered rows are not billed.

adults.title: Adults
adults.description: Adults in the room, 1 to 6, e.g. 2 (default 2). Google prices ONE room for the whole party: there is no rooms input, and above 6 adults Google returns no price at all. Rates scale with occupancy exactly as on Google, so compare like with like.

childrenAges.title: Children (ages)
childrenAges.description: Ages of the children in the same room, e.g. [5, 9] for two children aged 5 and 9. Empty (default) = no children. The price is for one room holding the adults plus these children.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 code for every price in the run, e.g. "EUR" (default "USD"): USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, THB, SGD, AUD, AED… When the user names no currency, pass the hotel's own ("EUR" for Lisbon). Every source's rate in the row is in this one currency.

country.title: Market
country.description: Google market (gl): any 2-letter country code, e.g. "gb", "pt", "jp" (default "us"). It is the country of the person booking, NOT the hotel's: keep "us" unless the user wants the parity picture as seen from a market. It changes which booking sites Google lists (Klook, Traveloka, Wego in Asian markets), so keep one market across a history.

language.title: Language
language.description: Google language (hl), e.g. "en", "de", "ja" (default "en"). Sets the language of hotel and source names where Google has a translation; hotelNames may be written in any language.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Keep the default (Apify datacenter proxies): Google accepts them for these calls, residential is unnecessary.

sessions.title: Parallel proxy sessions
sessions.description: Parallel proxy sessions, 1 to 16, e.g. 4 (default 4); each is paced at perIp requests per second. Raise for many hotels × stays, lower if Google throttles.

perIp.title: Requests per second per IP
perIp.description: Requests per second per proxy session, 0.1 to 2, e.g. 0.5 (default 0.5). 0.5 is safe; raise carefully.

description: Hotel rate parity checker on Google Hotels. Minimal input: {"hotelNames": ["Hyatt Regency Lisbon"], "checkIn": "30 days"}. One of hotelNames / hotels is required. One row per hotel and stay at $0.01, however many booking sites it holds; sweepDays multiplies the rows (6 = 7 stays per hotel), minSpreadPct delivers and bills only rows whose spread reaches N %.
